questions.question: The scientific discipline concerned with the study of drug origins, chemical properties, physiological mechanisms, and therapeutic applications is: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: Pharmacology is the comprehensive biomedical science dealing with the research, characterization, biological actions, and medical applications of chemical drugs on living biological systems.

questions.question: Any chemical substance that, when absorbed into the body of a living organism, alters normal physiological or biochemical function is defined as a: (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: In pharmacology, a drug is any biological or synthetic chemical agent (other than food providing nutritional support) that alters biochemical or physiological processes in an organism.

questions.question: Which powerful narcotic analgesic is naturally extracted from the latex resin of the opium poppy (Papaver somniferum)? (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: Morphine is a potent opioid analgesic alkaloid isolated from the dried latex of Papaver somniferum (opium poppy), prescribed under strict medical supervision for severe acute and post-surgical pain.

questions.question: The cardiotonic cardiac glycoside medication Digitalis (digoxin), used to strengthen myocardial contractions in heart failure, is extracted from which plant? (FBISE 2022)
questions.explanation: Digitalis (digoxin) is derived from the dried leaves of the purple foxglove (Digitalis purpurea). It inhibits cardiac sodium-potassium ATPase, increasing intracellular calcium and strengthening heart contractions.

questions.question: Which historic antimalarial medication was originally extracted from the natural bark of the South American Cinchona tree? (FBISE 2021)
questions.explanation: Quinine is a natural alkaloid extracted from the bark of the Cinchona tree that was historically the first effective clinical treatment for malaria caused by Plasmodium.

questions.question: Which widely used analgesic, antipyretic, and anti-inflammatory drug is completely synthesized chemically as acetylsalicylic acid? (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) is a synthetic non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that inhibits cyclooxygenase enzymes to relieve mild pain, reduce fever, and prevent blood platelet aggregation.

questions.question: Antibiotics that directly kill and destroy target bacterial cells are pharmacologically classified as: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: Bactericidal antibiotics (such as penicillins and cephalosporins) directly kill bacterial pathogens, typically by lysing cell walls or damaging cytoplasmic membranes.

questions.question: Antibiotics that inhibit the growth, reproduction, and metabolic replication of bacteria without killing them directly are termed: (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: Bacteriostatic antibiotics (such as tetracyclines and erythromycin) arrest bacterial cellular growth and protein synthesis, leaving the remaining immobilized bacteria to be eliminated by host immune phagocytes.

questions.question: Who discovered the first clinical antibiotic, penicillin, in 1928 after observing fungal contamination inhibiting bacterial growth on a petri dish? (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: Sir Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 when he noticed that colonies of Staphylococcus aureus were lysed around a contaminating mold colony of Penicillium notatum.

questions.question: Penicillin exerts its bactericidal antibacterial effect primarily by inhibiting the synthesis of which essential bacterial structure? (FBISE 2022)
questions.explanation: Penicillin selectively inhibits bacterial transpeptidase enzymes that cross-link peptidoglycan strands in the bacterial cell wall, causing growing bacteria to lyse under osmotic pressure.

questions.question: An antibiotic that is clinically active against a wide variety of both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacterial species is described as: (FBISE 2021)
questions.explanation: Broad-spectrum antibiotics (such as ampicillin and tetracycline) target fundamental mechanisms common to diverse pathogenic bacteria, killing both Gram-positive and Gram-negative strains.

questions.question: The progressive ability of pathogenic bacteria to survive and multiply despite exposure to standard therapeutic doses of antibiotics is termed: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: Antibiotic resistance develops when bacteria mutate or acquire resistance genes (e.g., via R-plasmids) encoding beta-lactamase enzymes or drug efflux pumps, rendering standard antibiotics ineffective.

questions.question: Which human behavioral practice is the primary leading cause driving the rapid global spread of antibiotic-resistant superbugs?

options.B: Overprescribing, misuse, and failing to complete prescribed courses of antibiotics

questions.explanation: Misuse of antibiotics for viral colds, premature discontinuation of courses, and excessive prophylactic antibiotic dosing in livestock create intense selection pressure that favors resistant mutant strains.

questions.question: Who pioneered the first successful vaccination in 1796 using cowpox fluid to immunize a boy against lethal smallpox? (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: Edward Jenner demonstrated in 1796 that inoculation with mild cowpox virus protected humans against deadly smallpox, laying the foundation for modern immunological vaccinology.

questions.question: A vaccine containing weakened (attenuated) or killed pathogenic antigens confers disease protection primarily by stimulating: (FBISE 2024)

options.B: Production of specific antibodies and long-lived immunological memory B and T cells

questions.explanation: Vaccines present harmless pathogen antigens to the immune system, inducing a primary immune response that produces protective antibodies and memory lymphocytes for rapid defense upon re-exposure.

questions.question: Which category of addictive psychoactive drugs depresses central nervous system activity, slows reaction time, and induces calm or drowsiness? (FBISE 2022)
questions.explanation: Sedatives (such as barbiturates and diazepam) depress neuronal transmission in the brain, reducing excitability, anxiety, and motor coordination, and inducing sleep.

questions.question: Drugs that alter sensory perception, causing individuals to see, hear, or feel vivid sensations that do not exist in reality, are termed: (FBISE 2021)
questions.explanation: Hallucinogens (such as mescaline, psilocybin, and LSD) distort sensory perception and emotional processing in the brain, provoking vivid visual and auditory hallucinations.

questions.question: Marijuana and hashish (charas) are psychoactive preparations derived from which plant species? (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: Marijuana and hashish are derived from the Indian hemp plant (Cannabis sativa). Their primary psychoactive ingredient is tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), which affects memory and cognition.

questions.question: Heroin is a highly addictive, illicit semi-synthetic opioid drug chemically synthesized from: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: Heroin (diacetylmorphine) is synthesized by acetylating morphine. It crosses the blood-brain barrier rapidly, producing euphoria and intense physical and psychological dependence.

questions.question: The physiological condition in which an individual requires progressively higher doses of a drug to produce the original pharmacological effect is called: (FBISE 2022)
questions.explanation: Drug tolerance occurs when repeated exposure diminishes the responsiveness of receptors or accelerates metabolic clearance, requiring larger doses to achieve the same initial effect.

questions.question: The distressing and often life-threatening physical and psychological symptoms that occur when an addicted person abruptly halts drug use are termed: (FBISE 2021)
questions.explanation: Withdrawal syndrome encompasses the adverse physiological and emotional disturbances (tremors, sweating, severe pain, convulsions) that manifest when a physically dependent user stops drug intake.

questions.question: Which of the following is a medicinal drug historically derived from animal sources prior to modern biotechnology?

options.A: Insulin from bovine and porcine pancreas

questions.explanation: Before recombinant DNA technology, therapeutic insulin was extracted from slaughtered bovine (cow) and porcine (pig) pancreases, and fish liver oil was extracted for vitamins A and D.

questions.question: Mineral sources supply which essential chemical used medically in tincture form as a potent topical skin antiseptic? (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: Iodine is a natural elemental mineral used as an antiseptic (in tincture of iodine or povidone-iodine) to disinfect skin surfaces and open wounds prior to surgical procedures.

questions.question: Which governmental vaccination initiative in Pakistan provides free immunization to infants against major childhood infectious diseases including polio, measles, and tuberculosis?
questions.explanation: Pakistans Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) aims to protect children under one year of age against vaccine-preventable killer diseases such as polio, diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, and measles.

questions.question: Chemical agents that are applied topically to living biological tissues (skin and wounds) to prevent or stop microbial infection are called: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: Antiseptics are non-toxic antimicrobial chemicals safe for application onto living human tissues and skin, unlike harsh disinfectants used exclusively on inanimate surfaces.

questions.question: Why are chemical disinfectants (such as household bleach and concentrated phenol) strictly restricted to inanimate surfaces?

options.A: They are completely ineffective against bacteria
options.B: They are highly cytotoxic and cause chemical burns and tissue destruction to living skin

questions.explanation: Disinfectants are powerful chemical agents formulated to sterilize floors, instruments, and bench tops; their caustic nature causes severe damage and burns to living animal tissues.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an analgesic medication?
questions.explanation: Analgesics are medications specifically designed to relieve pain without causing loss of consciousness, such as paracetamol, ibuprofen, and aspirin.

questions.question: The clinical condition known as Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) represents a dangerous medical threat because:

options.A: It is a superbug resistant to multiple standard beta-lactam antibiotics
options.B: It is a giant visible macroscopic worm
options.D: It can be cured with simple tap water

questions.explanation: MRSA is a hospital-acquired and community superbug that has evolved genetic resistance to methicillin and other common penicillin-family antibiotics, causing difficult-to-treat infections.

questions.question: Active acquired immunity differs from passive acquired immunity in that active immunity: (FBISE 2023)

options.A: Provides temporary protection that fades within two days
options.B: Involves the recipient own immune system producing antibodies and long-lived memory cells
options.D: Does not involve any lymphocytes or antigens

questions.explanation: Active immunity is stimulated when the hosts immune system encounters antigens (via infection or vaccination), generating long-lasting protective antibodies and memory cells.

questions.question: Administration of pre-formed antibodies (such as antivenom for snakebites or rabies immunoglobulin) provides which type of immunity?
questions.explanation: Antivenom provides immediate passive artificial immunity by supplying donor antibodies that neutralize toxins instantly, but confers no immunological memory and is cleared rapidly.

questions.question: Which hallucinogenic substance is naturally extracted from the small Mexican peyote cactus (Lophophora williamsii)?
questions.explanation: Mescaline is a naturally occurring psychedelic protoalkaloid obtained from the peyote cactus that induces altered states of consciousness and visual hallucinations.

questions.question: Psilocybin is an illicit hallucinogenic alkaloid naturally occurring in which biological source?

options.A: Certain species of wild mushrooms (magic mushrooms)

questions.explanation: Psilocybin is a natural psychedelic compound produced by over 200 species of fungi, commonly termed magic mushrooms or psilocybin mushrooms.

questions.question: Why are antibiotics completely ineffective against illnesses such as influenza, the common cold, and measles?

options.A: These illnesses are caused by viruses, which lack bacterial cellular structures and metabolism
options.C: Viruses destroy all antibiotics in the stomach
options.D: Antibiotics only work in cold weather

questions.explanation: Viruses lack peptidoglycan cell walls, ribosomes, and autonomous metabolic pathways targeted by antibiotics. Prescribing antibiotics for viral infections is completely ineffective and fuels drug resistance.

questions.question: Which of the following is an effective social measure to rehabilitate individuals recovering from chronic drug addiction?

options.B: Psychological counseling, medical detoxification, and vocational rehabilitation programs
options.C: Total social isolation in solitary confinement

questions.explanation: Successful addiction treatment requires compassionate multidisciplinary support: clinical detoxification to manage withdrawal, cognitive behavioral counseling, and vocational reintegration into society.

questions.question: The professional health field concerned directly with the compounding, formulation, and dispensing of medications to patients is: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: While pharmacology is the experimental study of drug action in living organisms, pharmacy is the applied clinical health science dedicated to preparing, dispensing, and ensuring the safe use of medications.
